title: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（3）
desc: 赴英留学生的残酷现实（3）

paragraphs.en: Kolluri mentioned that some of the subagents within the industry hardly even speak English. The same can be true of students themselves. Kapoor wondered how some of the students she worked with would cope in the UK.
paragraphs.zh: 科卢里提到，行业内一些次级代理几乎连英语都不会说。学生本身也可能如此。卡普尔想知道她合作过的一些学生将如何适应英国的生活。

paragraphs.en: "Their English was poor and their grades weren't great. How are you going to get through a master's degree when you can't write an essay?" To qualify for a student visa, applicants must pass an English test.
paragraphs.zh: "他们的英语很差，成绩也不好。当你连一篇论文都写不出来时，怎么能读完硕士学位呢？"为了获得学生签证资格，申请人必须通过英语测试。

paragraphs.en: But I spoke to several university lecturers who identified language as a real problem. "It's commonplace to have students who can barely speak English," one academic at a Russell Group university told me.
paragraphs.zh: 但我采访了几位大学讲师，他们认为语言确实是个问题。"有几乎不会说英语的学生是很常见的，"一位罗素集团大学的学者告诉我。

paragraphs.en: "They're clearly just there because the university wants their fees. It's so, so cynical." Another academic, from a top-ranked London university, told me: "I remember one Chinese student bursting into tears when I asked a question in a seminar, because she couldn't understand."
paragraphs.zh: "很明显，他们只是在那里，因为大学想要他们的学费。这太，太讽刺了。"另一位来自伦敦顶尖大学的学者告诉我："我记得有一次在研讨会上，当我问一个问题时，一个中国学生突然哭了，因为她听不懂。"

paragraphs.en: In the 2010s, British universities relied heavily on Chinese students, who by 2019 made up almost a third of all international students. But there was a persistent anxiety in government and within higher education that this over-reliance on a single country left universities highly exposed to geopolitical shifts.
paragraphs.zh: 2010年代，英国大学严重依赖中国学生，到2019年，中国学生几乎占所有国际学生的三分之一。但政府和高等教育界一直存在一种挥之不去的焦虑，即过度依赖一个国家会让大学极易受到地缘政治变化的影响。

paragraphs.en: As part of an effort to address this, in 2019, Boris Johnson announced a new work visa that would allow students to stay on for two years after completing their degree, without any restrictions on how much they had to earn or what kind of job they could do.
paragraphs.zh: 作为解决这一问题努力的一部分，2019年，鲍里斯•约翰逊宣布了一项新的工作签证，允许学生在完成学位后继续在英国停留两年，对他们必须挣多少钱或可以从事什么样的工作没有任何限制。

paragraphs.en: (A previous version of this visa was scrapped by Theresa May in 2012 on the grounds it was "too generous".) Johnson's visa change, which came into effect in mid-2021, brought the UK more in line with the US, Australia and Canada, its main competitors for international students. The message was clear: come here, study here, work here.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰逊的签证改革于2021年年中生效，使英国在吸引国际学生方面与主要竞争对手美国、澳大利亚和加拿大更加一致。其传达的信息是明确的：来这里学习，在这里工作。

paragraphs.en: Numbers of international students soared. The government had set the target of having 600,000 international students enrolled by 2030; this number was surpassed a decade ahead of schedule, and kept climbing, before peaking in 2022-23 at over 758,000.
paragraphs.zh: 国际学生的数量激增。政府设定的目标是到2030年招收60万名国际学生，这一目标提前10年就实现了，而且人数持续攀升，在2022-23学年达到峰值，超过75.8万人。

paragraphs.en: By 2022, India had displaced China as the single largest source of international students. Indian and Nigerian students, in particular, tended to be older than the typical Chinese student and often travelled with their families. After their graduate visas expired, many in this cohort obtained skilled worker visas by taking jobs as low-paid carers.
paragraphs.zh: 到2022年，印度已取代中国，成为国际学生的最大来源国。特别是印度和尼日利亚的学生，他们往往比典型的中国学生年龄更大，而且经常与家人一起旅行。在研究生签证到期后，这个群体中的许多人通过从事低薪护理工作获得了技术工人签证。

paragraphs.en: As net migration figures shot up, the mood in Westminster soured. The Conservative government responded by first restricting students from bringing their families with them, then introducing a minimum salary threshold of £38,700 for a skilled worker visa – a near 50% increase.
paragraphs.zh: 随着净移民人数激增，英国议会的气氛变得紧张起来。保守党政府首先限制留学生携带家属，随后将技术工人签证的最低工资门槛提高到38700英镑，涨幅近50%。

paragraphs.en: When Labour came into power in 2024, they increased the threshold again to £41,700, and announced plans to reduce the post-study work visa from two years to 18 months.
paragraphs.zh: 2024年工党上台后，再次将门槛提高到41700英镑，并宣布计划将毕业生工作签证从两年缩短至18个月。

paragraphs.en: The promise implied in a lot of international student recruitment is that students can stay on and work after graduation, but this is becoming harder and harder.
paragraphs.zh: 许多国际招生宣传中隐含的承诺——学生毕业后可以留下来工作——正变得越来越难以实现。

paragraphs.en: When Sam accepted an offer for a master's degree in finance at the University of Dundee in 2023, he took out a loan of £25,000 to cover the £17,000 university fees, plus other costs. This was more than five times his annual salary. His family did not have any assets to secure it against, which meant a higher interest rate.
paragraphs.zh: 2023年，萨姆接受了邓迪大学金融硕士的录取通知，并贷款2.5万英镑来支付1.7万英镑的学费及其他费用。这笔贷款超过他年收入的五倍。由于他的家庭没有任何资产作为抵押，这意味着他需要支付更高的利率。

paragraphs.en: Six months after graduation, fixed monthly repayments of £300 would begin. That was almost his entire monthly salary in India, but Sam calculated that if he could get a job in the UK paying at least £25,000 during his two years on a graduate visa, he'd be able to pay off a significant chunk of the loan.
paragraphs.zh: 毕业后六个月，他需要开始每月固定还款300英镑。这几乎是他在印度时的全部月薪，但萨姆盘算着，如果能在两年的毕业生签证期间在英国找到一份年薪至少2.5万英镑的工作，他就能还清大部分贷款。

paragraphs.en: "I was in a delusion that I'd get a job really easily," Sam said. What he didn't realise was that the terms of the deal he was accepting – debt now, opportunity later – had already been reset by decisions made in Westminster.
paragraphs.zh: "我曾幻想自己会轻松找到工作，"山姆说。他未曾意识到，自己接受的"先负债后机遇"的交易条件，早已因威斯敏斯特的决策而被重置。

paragraphs.en: Many prospective international students see Britain as a place of wealth and opportunity, so it can be a shock to arrive and be confronted by a housing crisis and a brutal job market. In January 2022, a young man called Ajith (not his real name) started a master's in digital marketing at Oxford Brookes University.
paragraphs.zh: 许多有意向的留学生将英国视为财富与机遇之地，因此当他们抵达后，面对住房危机和残酷的就业市场时，可能会感到震惊。2022年1月，一位名叫阿吉斯（化名）的年轻人开始在牛津布鲁克斯大学攻读数字营销硕士学位。

paragraphs.en: Ajith, who came from a village in Tamil Nadu, was 24 and frustrated he wasn't getting the kind of jobs he wanted in India. He secured a loan against his family's agricultural land.
paragraphs.zh: 阿吉斯来自泰米尔纳德邦的一个村庄，当时24岁，他因在印度找不到理想的工作而感到沮丧。他以家里的农业用地为抵押获得了贷款。

paragraphs.en: According to Ajith, his education agent, from StudyIn, had told him that "getting part-time work to support myself while studying is easy, finding accommodation is easy and finding a job afterwards is easy".
paragraphs.zh: 据阿吉斯说，他的留学中介StudyIn曾告诉他，在学习期间找兼职工作养活自己很容易，找住处很容易，毕业后找工作也很容易。
